title: Promise finance the shape of fct_order_lines

ticket.subject: Our reconciliation broke again after a refactor
body: Our month-end reconciliation reads `fct_order_lines` directly. Last month a refactor turned `net_amount` into
a floating-point number and the totals stopped matching the ledger by a few cents; nobody noticed until the
close. The time before, someone "fixed" the discount so it applied to each unit instead of once per line.
1. Make the shape of `fct_order_lines` a promise dbt enforces at build time: exactly the columns it has
today, with their types, and `net_amount` as an exact `decimal(12,2)`. A change that breaks it must fail
2. Pin the `net_amount` rule (quantity × unit price, minus the line's discount taken once) with a test that
does not depend on the data of the day, so the next refactor cannot change it silently.
The landing tables are already loaded. Run the whole project when you are done.

acceptance.text: fct_order_lines has an enforced contract that declares every column's type, net_amount as decimal(12,2).
The table in the warehouse has exactly those columns and types, and the same rows.

checks.sql: SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'dbt_dev_contract' AND table_name = 'fct_order_lines'
checks.fail: The built table does not have the promised columns and types.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_lines, CAST(sum(net_amount) AS DOUBLE) AS net_total FROM dbt_dev_contract.fct_order_lines
checks.fail: The table's rows or totals changed.

acceptance.text: A dbt unit test on stg_shop__order_lines pins net_amount with rows of its own, and it passes.
Your last dbt command was a dbt build of the whole project, and everything passed.

hints: dbt calls this promise a model contract: `contract: {enforced: true}` in the model's config, and a `data_type` on every column.
With an enforced contract dbt checks the query's columns and types before it builds the table. What type does `quantity * unit_price - discount_amount` have in DuckDB?
A dbt unit test (`unit_tests:` in a YAML file) gives a model hand-written input rows and the rows it must return; `dbt build` runs it before the model.
Give the unit test at least one line with a quantity above 1 and a discount: that is the row that tells the two formulas apart.
